title: health check api returns server status and timestamp
description: Test GET /api/health endpoint to verify it returns a 200 status with a JSON object containing status, message, and timestamp fields indicating the server is running.

title: authentication api login with valid credentials
description: Test POST /api/auth/login with valid username and password to ensure it returns a 200 status with a JWT token and user object containing id, username, fullName, and role.

title: authentication api login with invalid credentials returns 401
description: Test POST /api/auth/login with invalid username or password to verify it returns a 401 status with an error message.

title: authentication api get current user with valid token
description: Test GET /api/auth/me with a valid Authorization Bearer token to confirm it returns a 200 status with the authenticated user object containing id, username, fullName, role.

title: authentication api get current user without token returns 401
description: Test GET /api/auth/me without Authorization header to verify it returns a 401 status.

title: authentication api logout with valid token
description: Test POST /api/auth/logout with a valid Authorization Bearer token to ensure it returns a 200 status with a logout acknowledgement message.

title: user management list users with admin token
description: Test GET /api/users with a valid admin Authorization Bearer token to verify it returns a 200 status with { users: [...] } array, no password hashes in any user object.

title: user management create user with admin token
description: Test POST /api/users with admin token and body { username, password, fullName, role }. THE RESPONSE IS ALWAYS WRAPPED: { 'user': { id, username, fullName, role, isActive } }. Python code to get id: data = resp.json(); user_obj = data['user']; user_id = user_obj['id']. Do NOT do resp.json()['id'] — that will fail. Expect 201. Clean up by deleting the created user.

title: user management update user fields with admin token
description: Step 1: POST /api/users to create test user. RESPONSE IS WRAPPED: data = create_resp.json(); user_obj = data['user']; user_id = user_obj['id']. Step 2: PUT /api/users/:id with { fullName, role }. RESPONSE IS ALSO WRAPPED: data = update_resp.json(); updated = data['user']; assert updated['fullName'] == new_name. Step 3: DELETE test user. NEVER call resp.json()['id'] — ALWAYS go through resp.json()['user']['id'].

title: user management deactivate and reactivate user account with admin token
description: Step 1: POST /api/users. RESPONSE WRAPPED: user_id = create_resp.json()['user']['id']. Step 2: PATCH /api/users/:id/status with { isActive: False }. RESPONSE WRAPPED: patched = patch_resp.json()['user']; assert patched['isActive'] == False. Step 3: PATCH again with { isActive: True }; assert patch2_resp.json()['user']['isActive'] == True. Step 4: DELETE user. Always use .json()['user'] to unwrap.

title: vendor management list active vendors returns vendors array
description: Test GET /api/vendors with a valid Bearer token. Expect 200 with { vendors: [...] }. An empty array is acceptable. If vendors exist, each should have id, vendorCode, vendorName fields.

title: vendor csv import preview returns rows and errors array without db write
description: Test POST /api/vendors/import/preview with admin Bearer token. Multipart/form-data, field name must be 'file'. Build CSV in Python: csv_content = 'vendor_code,vendor_name,contact_person,phone,email,payment_terms,notes\nVC001,Test Vendor,,,,,' and send as files={'file': ('v.csv', csv_content.encode(), 'text/csv')}. Expect 200 with EXACTLY these two keys: { 'rows': [...], 'errors': [] }. The key is 'errors' NOT 'validationErrors'. There is NO 'previewId' field. Do not assert previewId exists.

title: vendor csv import commit inserts vendors and returns inserted count
description: Test POST /api/vendors/import with admin Bearer token. This endpoint takes a JSON body (NOT multipart, NO previewId). EXACT Python code: payload = {'rows': [{'vendor_code': 'TEST_V_TC013', 'vendor_name': 'Test Vendor TC013', 'contact_person': '', 'phone': '', 'email': '', 'payment_terms': '', 'notes': ''}]}; resp = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers). Expect 200 with {'inserted': N}. Assert 'inserted' in resp.json() and isinstance(resp.json()['inserted'], int).

title: item management list active items returns items array
description: Test GET /api/items with a valid Bearer token. Expect 200 with { items: [...] }. An empty array is acceptable. If items exist, each should have id, itemCode, description fields.

title: item csv import preview returns rows and errors array without db write
description: Test POST /api/items/import/preview with admin Bearer token. Multipart/form-data, field name 'file'. CSV: 'item_code,description,category,unit_of_measure,min_quantity,max_quantity,lead_time_days,safety_stock,notes\nITEM001,Test Item,Cat,EA,5,100,14,2,'. Expect 200 with { 'rows': [...], 'errors': [] }. The key is 'errors' NOT 'validationErrors'. There is NO previewId field.

title: item csv import commit inserts items and returns inserted count
description: Test POST /api/items/import with admin Bearer token. WARNING: This endpoint does NOT use previewId. Send a JSON body directly. EXACT Python code to use: payload = {'rows': [{'item_code': 'TEST_ITEM_TC016', 'description': 'Test Item TC016', 'category': 'Test', 'unit_of_measure': 'EA', 'min_quantity': '5', 'max_quantity': '100', 'lead_time_days': '14', 'safety_stock': '2', 'notes': ''}]}; resp = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers); assert resp.status_code == 200; data = resp.json(); assert 'inserted' in data; assert isinstance(data['inserted'], int). Do NOT send previewId or confirm fields.

title: transaction receipt create stores receipt and returns transaction with last paid price
description: Test POST /api/transactions/receipts. IMPORTANT STEPS: Step 1 — commit vendor: POST /api/vendors/import with json={'rows': [{'vendor_code': 'RCPT_VND_TC017', 'vendor_name': 'Vendor TC017', 'contact_person': '', 'phone': '', 'email': '', 'payment_terms': '', 'notes': ''}]}, expect 200. Step 2 — commit item: POST /api/items/import with json={'rows': [{'item_code': 'RCPT_ITM_TC017', 'description': 'Item TC017', 'category': 'Test', 'unit_of_measure': 'EA', 'min_quantity': '0', 'max_quantity': '999', 'lead_time_days': '14', 'safety_stock': '0', 'notes': ''}]}, expect 200. Step 3 — get IDs: GET /api/vendors find vendorCode=='RCPT_VND_TC017'; GET /api/items find itemCode=='RCPT_ITM_TC017'. Step 4 — POST /api/transactions/receipts with EXACTLY these camelCase fields: {'itemId': item_id, 'vendorId': vendor_id, 'location': 'ADEL', 'quantity': 5, 'unitCost': 10.00, 'transactionDate': '2026-01-15T00:00:00.000Z'}. Expect 200 (NOT 201) with {'transaction': {id, transactionType: 'RECEIPT'}, 'lastPaidPrice': null or number}.

title: transaction stock position returns aggregated quantities by item and location
description: Test GET /api/transactions/stock-position with Bearer token. Expect 200 with { positions: [...] }. Each position has: item (object with id, itemCode), adelQty (number), calhounQty (number), totalQty (number). An empty array is valid.

title: transaction history returns filtered list of transactions
description: Test GET /api/transactions with Bearer token. Call without filters: expect 200 with { transactions: [...] }. Then call with ?location=ADEL: expect 200. Then call with ?type=RECEIPT: expect 200. Each transaction object has a nested item object. An empty array is valid.

title: dashboard stats returns aggregated counts
description: Test GET /api/dashboard/stats with Bearer token. Expect 200 with { totalItems: number, transactionsMTD: number, activeVendors: number, teamMembers: number }. All values must be non-negative integers (or 0).

title: dashboard low stock returns flat items below minimum quantity
description: Test GET /api/dashboard/low-stock with Bearer token. Expect 200 with { items: [...] }. An empty array is valid. IMPORTANT: Each entry is a FLAT object — there is NO nested 'item' sub-object. Fields are directly on the entry: id (number), itemCode (string), description (string), category (string), currentStock (number), minQuantity (number), burnRate (number or null), daysRemaining (number or null). Assert entry['id'] and entry['itemCode'] directly, NOT entry['item']['id'].

title: dashboard dead stock returns flat items with no recent activity
description: Test GET /api/dashboard/dead-stock with Bearer token. Expect 200 with { items: [...] }. An empty array is valid. Each entry is a FLAT object: id (number), itemCode (string), description (string), category (string), currentStock (number). No nested 'item' sub-object.

title: dashboard valuation returns inventory value by location
description: Test GET /api/dashboard/valuation with Bearer token. Expect 200 with { adel: number, calhoun: number, total: number }. All values non-negative. total must equal adel + calhoun within 0.01 tolerance.

title: dashboard activity feed returns recent transactions with human readable descriptions
description: Test GET /api/dashboard/activity with Bearer token. Expect 200 with { activity: [...] }. Array length <= 20. An empty array is valid. IMPORTANT: Each entry has these exact fields: id (number), description (non-empty string), transactionType (string — NOT 'type'), location (string), transactionDate (string), createdAt (string). Assert entry['transactionType'] NOT entry['type'].
